A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AstroLoc research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material are readable and support comparison across the revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original AstroLoc localization results, training ablations, feature-dimensionality experiments, and qualitative analyses, including historical imagery and nanosatellite localization.

after.justification: V2 retains original AstroLoc benchmark and supplementary results and reports additional sampling-control results in Table 6.

M1.justification: The footprint-labeling pipeline, query-satellite pair loss, query-weighted satellite clustering, MUM loss, and model architectures remain unchanged. Section 4.3 reorganizes the explanation into three sampling solutions; the additional controls do not change the final AstroLoc procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same astronaut and satellite training data, six original and extended regional benchmarks, worldwide search, VINSat queries, and historical Space Shuttle imagery. Removing California-L from the ablation table does not remove it from the paper's evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. Table 6 adds naive-sampling comparison variants, alone and combined with the pair loss. V1's MS loss with default mining and MUM loss remain as Solutions 2 and 3.

E3.justification: V2 adds controlled training comparisons using unclustered random quadruplet sampling, with and without the pair loss, and no longer reports the small/base backbone feature-dimensionality sweep. Retained experiments keep the same splits, training budgets, hyperparameters, rotation augmentation, and recall metrics.

E4.justification: The supporting analyses are substantially reshaped: Table 6 adds two naive-sampling controls but removes California-L ablations. V1's feature-size sensitivity study, geographic cluster-weight map, and t-SNE mining diagnostic are removed rather than relocated. The supplementary qualitative examples and failure-case analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's additional ablation rows retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 and 7, and matched entries in Table 6, have identical values. New Table 6 controls report Texas-L recall@1 of 67.6 for naive sampling and 84.0 for pair loss plus naive sampling. California-L ablation scores and the feature-dimensionality results are removed.

T1.justification: V2 drops v1's explicit batch and quadruplet definition in Section 4.3, Eq. 7, although the batch notation still appears in the MUM loss. The uniform-sampling equation is also omitted in favor of prose. The loss formulas and weighted-sampling probabilities otherwise remain mathematically unchanged.

C1.justification: The principal localization, performance, and transfer claims are retained. V2 strengthens the miner's novelty claim: the introduction calls it the first of its kind, and Section 4.3 claims it is the only mining technique using one distribution to learn how to sample another.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 and the new Figure 5 explicitly argue that uninformative desert or sea batches can harm learning, sharpening the earlier distribution-mismatch rationale. The feature-dimensionality discussion connecting accuracy, memory, and search time is removed. Supplementary forest, coast, and cloud failure-mode interpretations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-site link on the title page and removes v1's explicit promise to make the precise localization labels available. Technical settings remain stable; the 5,000-iteration mining refresh interval and less-than-10% training overhead are relocated to Section 5.1.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to GSV-Cities, FoundLoc, Ge et al.'s region-similarity work, and Trivigno et al.'s camera-pose refinement work. It also emphasizes the miner's distinctiveness more strongly, while retaining the main astronaut-localization and UAV research positioning.

P1.justification: Section 4.3 is extensively rewritten into a progression from naive sampling through clustering to unsupervised mining. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are revised, contribution bullets are removed, implementation prose is relocated, and the references move after the supplementary discussion.

P2.justification: V2 adds the sampling-batch comparison in Figure 5, redraws the pipeline illustration, annotates the coverage plot, and removes v1's cluster map, t-SNE plot, and feature-size plot. Table 6 becomes a component-checkmark matrix. The retained supplementary image panels are renumbered and rearranged alongside the references.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the mining explanation and adds useful controls separating naive sampling from clustering and query-weighted mining. However, it removes the feature-dimensionality study, California-L ablations, and two mining diagnostics, reducing analytical completeness. With the core benchmark results unchanged, these benefits and losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
